Shop made in USA wool blankets & throws from Pendleton. Fine wool throw blankets woven in America for over a century. Sourced through wool-grower partnerships that in some cases go back over a hundred years, wool is a naturally renewable, biodegradable fiber that acts as a natural heat regulator, insulating against both cold and heat while resisting stains and wrinkles. From the softness of Eco-Wise Wool® to our traditional jacquard weaves, each blanket blends heritage design with everyday durability. Pendleton wool blankets are well known for their bold patterns and vibrant color combinations. Many of these designs draw inspiration from the American West and are rooted in Pendleton's century-old archives. Where are Pendleton blankets made? Most Pendleton wool blankets are woven in Pendleton's historic Pacific Northwest mills in Oregon and Washington. Our jacquard-patterned wool blankets are woven at our original mill in Pendleton, Oregon, which has been producing blankets since 1909. What is the difference between "napped" and "unnapped" on a wool blanket? Napped wool has been brushed to raise the fiber ends from the weave, creating a softer, thicker feel. An unnapped blanket has not been combed so the pattern is sharper with cleaner edges.
